questions.q: What Snowflake data type holds the ticketing API's raw JSON payload?
options: ARRAY
VARIANT
OBJECT
VARCHAR
questions.explain: VARIANT is Snowflake's native type for semi-structured data like JSON, held untouched until parsed.

questions.q: Why does this pipeline land the JSON untouched first, instead of extracting fields during the COPY INTO step?
options: Snowflake's COPY INTO command cannot read JSON files at all
It's not actually a deliberate choice — extracting fields during load would be equally valid
A change in the source JSON's shape then only affects the later parsing step, not the load step itself
VARIANT columns are required by Snowflake's licensing terms
questions.explain: Landing raw JSON first decouples ingestion from parsing, so a renamed or added field in the source only requires fixing the parsing step, not the load mechanism.

questions.q: What does the FILE_FORMAT option in this lesson's COPY INTO statement specify?
options: TYPE = JSON
TYPE = AVRO
TYPE = PARQUET
TYPE = CSV
questions.explain: The ticketing API exports JSON, so the COPY INTO command uses FILE_FORMAT = (TYPE = JSON).

questions.q: What does ON_ERROR = 'ABORT_STATEMENT' do during a COPY INTO load?
options: Fails the entire load if any row is malformed, instead of silently skipping it
Emails an alert but still loads every valid row
Deletes the source file after a failed load
Automatically fixes malformed JSON rows
questions.explain: ABORT_STATEMENT stops the whole load on a bad row, so a malformed record fails loudly instead of quietly going missing.

questions.q: In the sample export shown in this lesson, why is refund_amount null on most rows?
options: Most tickets never involve a refund at all — Finance's view only cares about the rows where it isn't null
The ticketing API never actually sends a refund_amount field
null means the JSON failed to parse
Snowflake automatically sets numeric fields to null on odd-numbered rows
questions.explain: Refunds are the exception, not the rule — refund_amount is populated only on the subset of tickets where a refund actually happened.
